rounds.text: Institutional confidence in Kabra Jewels Ltd is actively evaporating, as demonstrated by foreign institutions slashing their holding from 3.28% to 0.00% and domestic institutions cutting theirs from 1.89% to 0.11% by March 2026 [E2, E3]. This sharp exodus drives a negative institutional money flow signal that directly underpins a modest 49 out of 100 rules-based screen score [E4, E7, E8]. Operationally, the business faces structural margin compression, with EBITDA margins dropping from 16% in November to 13% in March due to rising metal prices that cannot be fully passed on to consumers [E21, E27]. Furthermore, management explicitly admitted that April and May sales were severely slowed by high gold prices, while the diamond segment suffered a temporary contraction from the rise of the lab-grown market [E14, E16]. Conceded: the consumer durables sector enjoys a positive tailwind with strong median sales and profit growth [E10, E11, E12]. Despite these sector tailwinds, the company defers external debt reduction for another two to three years while sitting on INR11.5 crores of unutilized IPO funds, leaving the risk profile unsupported by the current valuation [E24, E26].
